label: AFFECTION

cover.headline: How to ask for affection *without feeling needy*
cover.sub: 5 ways to say what you want.

points.heading: Wanting closeness is normal
points.body: Needing affection isn’t a flaw. It’s part of being close to someone.
points.panel: Notice one moment this week when you wanted a hug, and let that be okay.

points.heading: Ask for something specific
points.body: “More affection” is hard to act on. A small, clear ask is easy to say yes to.
points.panel: “Would you hold my hand when we walk tonight?”

points.heading: Ask, don’t accuse
points.body: “You never touch me” starts a defense. A request starts a connection.
points.panel: “I really love it when you hug me from behind.”

points.heading: Thank him when it happens
points.body: Noticing the effort makes it more likely to happen again.
points.panel: “That hug this morning made my whole day.”

points.heading: Ask what he likes too
points.body: Affection goes both ways, and his favorite kind may surprise you.
points.panel: “What’s a way I show love that you really like?”

close.save: Save this for when it feels hard to ask.

caption:
Many women feel embarrassed asking for affection, as if needing it means something is wrong.

It doesn’t. Wanting closeness is part of loving someone. The trick is asking in a way that’s easy to say yes to: small, specific, and kind. Here are five ways to do it.

Save this for when it feels hard to ask, and follow @spotseason for more.
